_README: Pre-registered gate thresholds. gates.py reads ONLY this file, so a threshold
cannot be adjusted after seeing a result without the change appearing in git.
REVISION 1 (recorded, not hidden): the G1 thresholds below replace the ones in
de_xuat_kd_2_SCD_giao_thuc.md S3.3. The originals asked for a MARGINAL win of
the product over fidelity alone. Running the synthetic gate showed that
Theorem 1 does not predict that: it is a product of two factors, so it predicts
a REGIME. Where capacity binds, fidelity on mu already predicts and coverage
adds nothing; where capacity is ample, fidelity on the real corpus goes blind
(exactly zero loss with a large capability gap) and coverage carries all the
signal. The synthetic stage is therefore EXPLORATORY and its output is the
hypothesis the GPU stages test. The original thresholds are kept in
g1.superseded_thresholds so the change is auditable.
REVISION 2 (recorded, not hidden): GP.1 is demoted from a gate to a diagnostic.
Its 8-point threshold was calibrated by analogy with an earlier run whose base
student scored 34.6% on GSM8K alone; the first real GP run had a base of 41.3%
on a pooled suite, because the chat template and the forced-cue protocol are
better. An absolute threshold in accuracy points on a quantity whose ceiling is
set by the configuration is not well-posed, and GP did not even measure the
ceiling. The fix is not a smaller number: it is (a) GP now evaluates the teacher
so Gamma and private-value recovery are measured, and (b) the gate is the
headroom criterion GP.6, which has an actual derivation (S9.4: the reliability
of the dependent variable caps the observable correlation regardless of whether
the hypothesis is true). GP.1's old value is kept in gp.superseded_thresholds.
Note this does NOT make the first run pass: GP.6 failed too, at 1.6x against a
required 4x. The headroom problem is real and is not a threshold problem.
REVISION 3 (recorded): G3 gains a capacity probe, G3.0. The synthetic stage
found the coverage effect is regime-dependent -- absent where capacity binds,
dominant where it does not -- and stage GP then measured the 0.5B student
recovering only 47.5% of a 65.6-point gap, i.e. the capacity-limited end. A
null result there would not distinguish a wrong theory from a wrong regime, so
G3 now trains one identity-measure arm per student first and stops if the
recovery spread across students is under 15 points. This is a design
precondition, not a hypothesis test: it decides whether the 25 GPU-hour
comparison is interpretable at all.
REVISION 4 (recorded): gate G0 now decides per estimator instead of failing the
whole stage, and its accuracy criterion is restricted to configurations the
estimator can represent. Neither is a threshold change.
(a) The pre-registered decision rule (design doc S2.5) says that when the
estimators disagree the response is 'continue with estimator A alone,
treat B and C as reference'. The gate instead failed the stage outright,
which does not implement that rule -- the same class of harness bug as the
verdict predicate in revision 2.
(b) The accuracy criterion compared a clipped estimator against an unclipped
reference. Both estimators clip the per-state density ratio at 50, so the
coefficient they can report is bounded far below the exact value, which
reaches 98,208 on the hole family. For the 36.5% of configurations above
that range the +/-20% test fails by construction. In range: A 0.93,
B 0.89. Pooled, as first reported: A 0.74, B 0.56. Both are printed.
The first real run's verdict under the old wiring was FAIL on 2 of 15. Under the
new wiring estimator C is dropped -- its rank disagreement with A (0.643) was
checked for a tie artefact and is real, no estimate reached the clip -- while A
is admissible and corroborated by B at 0.868, so identification (C5) holds.
REVISION 5 (recorded): gate G2 now blocks on estimator A's own behaviour instead
of failing the stage when estimator B fails. Design doc S4.5 fixed these
responses in advance and all three failures map to one of them: G2.3 -> 'drop B
and C, use A alone, UNLESS G2.7 also fails, then stop'; G2.1 -> 'if unfixable,
use A only'; G2.6 -> 'use A only, remove B and C from the paper'. The one
criterion whose failure the protocol made a stop condition, G2.5, passed at
+0.187, and G2.7 passed at CV 0.015.
Thresholds applied to A are BORROWED, not invented after seeing its values:
- null and paraphrase bands = g2.w1_c2_lo/hi = [0.90, 1.15], registered here
for the null calibration of the coverage estimate; both tests require 1.
- sensitivity bar = g3.c2_spread_min_ratio = 1.5, registered for 'the
intervention moves C2', the same question W5 asks.
Measured: A null 1.047, paraphrase 1.009, real shift 2.842, separation 2.71x.
IDENTIFICATION DID NOT SURVIVE AS DESIGNED. Criterion C5 wanted two estimators
agreeing in rank; none qualifies in both worlds (synthetic: A~B 0.868, A~C 0.643;
real text: A~C 0.800, A~B 0.600). A rests instead on validation against an
exactly computable ground truth in G0 plus four behavioural checks on real text.
That is a different claim from 'C5 satisfied' and the paper must make it in those
words.
REVISION 6 (recorded): G6 gains a precondition, G6.0, and a new way to build its
deficient measure. The first run was NOT interpretable: cluster_drop bans cells
rarest-first until 1-frac of the count mass is gone, and at frac=0.25 the cell
distribution is steep enough that it left ONE cell of the 413 the teacher visits.
From a single cell any diverse addition of 4000 prefixes covers 300-400 cells, so
which prefix a rule picks stops mattering: random reached held-out C2 1.797 and
the ratio rule 1.912. That is not a refutation of Proposition 2, it is a broken
manipulation, and the log printed n_states_seen_mu = 1 the whole time.
cell_drop now drops a random 1-frac of the CELLS, leaving partial coverage, and
G6 refuses to run the sweep unless the measure covers 20-80% of the teacher's
cells. Worth recording separately: even in the invalid test the ratio rule did
not beat random (0.997x) while rarest_cell (1.017x) and uniform_cell (1.015x)
did marginally. That is a warning about Proposition 2's prescription, not yet
evidence against it.
REVISION 7 (recorded): G6 sweeps the branch budget instead of fixing it at 4000,
and refuses to run when the largest budget exceeds half the coupon-collector
threshold. The arithmetic forced this. The first VALID run (measure covering
170 of 413 cells, 41.2%) still could not discriminate: covering n cells by
random draws needs about n*ln(n) = 2488 draws, so a budget of 4000 is 1.6x the
threshold and random selection covers nearly everything. Measured cell counts
confirm it -- 334 to 408 of 413 for every rule -- and every held-out coefficient
landed between 1.23 and 1.60 from a starting 22.26.
Results of that run, kept because they are real even though the test could not
discriminate: rarest_cell 1.016x random, uniform_cell 1.013x, random 1.000x,
ratio (Proposition 2) 0.998x, deficit_cell 0.998x. Two of the three alternatives
the design registered for this situation are still untried: student entropy, and
k-center on hidden-state features -- the latter no longer available because G2
dropped that estimator. So G6 is not yet a refutation of Proposition 2, but the
prescription has now failed to beat random on two different measures.
G6 OUTCOME (recorded, no threshold touched): Proposition 2 is REFUTED, and the
refutation is clean -- both preconditions passed (measure covering 41.2% of the
teacher's cells; largest budget 0.32x the coupon-collector threshold), four
budgets spanning the scarce regime, six rules including all the alternatives the
design registered for this situation.
Best reduction ratio anywhere: 1.0235x (rarest_cell at budget 800). Bar: 1.5x.
At the scarcest budget RANDOM IS THE BEST RULE and every targeted rule is worse:
entropy 0.607x, uniform_cell 0.662x, rarest_cell 0.836x, ratio 0.994x.
Mechanism, which makes this more than a null: C2 weights by the teacher's mass
(sum d^2/mu), so chasing rare or deficient cells spends the budget where the
teacher barely goes. Proposition 2's rule carries the d factor and so avoids that
trap -- it tracks random instead of being harmed by targeting -- but it cannot
beat random either, because the candidate prefixes are already drawn FROM teacher
traces and are therefore already d-distributed. When the pool is already drawn
from the right measure, coverage expansion is self-targeting and there is nothing
left to aim. ratio and deficit_cell returned byte-identical numbers at all four
budgets, so the derived rule and a counting heuristic are the same selector.
What this does and does not kill. Theorem 1 (0/780 violations), Corollary 1.1
(47 configurations, gap 0.523 at exactly zero fidelity loss), and estimator A
(validated against ground truth in G0, behaviourally in G2) are untouched: they
are about measuring coverage, not about aiming a budget. G5 as designed is now
pointless -- its method arm and its random-prefix control are provably the same
thing. G3 is not: it manipulates mu by masking, never uses Proposition 2, and is
the test of whether the measure outweighs the objective on real models.
REVISION 8 (recorded, not hidden): G4 is EXTENDED, not re-thresholded.
The first G4 run swept 5 pairs x 3 measures = 15 points and missed G4.1:
rho(product)=+0.343 against the registered +0.60. All four validity conditions
passed (reliability 0.998, design ceiling 0.948, C2 spread 38.8x, predictor
collinearity -0.353, positive-gain fraction 1.00), so the design is sound and
the shortfall is not an artefact of a homogeneous grid. What the three failures
share is a power signature rather than a wrong sign: the product still beats
fidelity (-0.043) by a gap of +0.386, and the partial regression puts the
coverage term at p=5.43e-02 -- just outside 0.05 -- with the predicted sign.
With n=15, Williams p=0.347 cannot resolve a gap of that size whatever the
truth is. The extension therefore adds PAIRS, which is the axis the stage
exists to vary: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct joins the teacher list, for up to 3 more
pairs and n=24. NO THRESHOLD IS CHANGED, and the dropped pair
3B <- 3B-Instruct stays dropped (Gamma=9.8 < 10.0) because relaxing a validity
filter after seeing a failure is the move this file exists to prevent. If G4.1
still misses at n=24, the registered failure action stands and G4 is reported
as a negative result: a bound that holds and does not transfer.
REVISION 9 (recorded, not hidden): three things, two of them post hoc and
labelled as such, one of them prospective.
(a) G7 POST HOC. The stage called coverage_of(rows, rows), comparing the
supervision with itself, so it recorded C2 = 1.00 for all ten configurations and
could not see that the sweep moves C2 from 8.35 down to 1.01. Recomputing C2
against the teacher's own trace pool, from the cached corpora and with no model
retrained, is a DECLARED POST-HOC measurement. The pre-registered G7 endpoint
was the ratio of regression coefficients on distinct cells versus prompt count;
that criterion FAILED at 2.69 against a 3.0 bar, and validity condition V8
FAILED at 42 cells against a 200 bar. G7 is reported as not passing. What the
recomputation adds is five new points on the coverage axis, all of them in the
benign regime, and the observation that accuracy is flat for C2 <= 9 and falls
off a cliff after it. That is a hypothesis for a future stage, not a result of
this one.
(b) G4 POST HOC. Within each of the five pairs, mean gain is strictly monotone
decreasing in C2 -- 5 pairs out of 5, no exceptions. The pooled rank test is
nevertheless weak (rho_product = +0.343) because gains range from +7.24 to
+63.69 across pairs, driven by the available headroom Gamma and not by coverage:
a badly covered arm of a high-headroom pair outranks a well covered arm of a
low-headroom pair. The pooled endpoint was the wrong statistic for a blocked
design. This diagnosis is post hoc and the registered G4.1 verdict stands.
(c) PROSPECTIVE, for the extension still running. Before any 14B pair has
produced a result, the endpoint for the extended G4 is registered here as a
WITHIN-PAIR test: Gamma-normalised recovery, and the count of pairs whose three
measures come out in the predicted order. Bar: at least 7 of 8 pairs ordered
correctly. The pooled rho_product criterion is kept and reported alongside; it
is not replaced, so both numbers appear whatever happens.
(d) A SECOND G4 ARM IS ADDED, with its own ledger: objective = ce. G3 showed
that forward KL is far more robust to poor coverage than a hard label (at the
worst measure, 60.39% under fkl against 8.19% under ce for the 1.5B student), so
running G4 under fkl compresses exactly the contrast G4 exists to detect. The ce
arm uses the same five cached pairs and the same registered thresholds.
REVISION 10 (recorded, not hidden): a new stage G9 is registered, with the
thresholds in the g9 block above written BEFORE any arm ran.
Why it exists. G3 measured C2 at 1.02, 5.36, 14.47 and 39.15; G7's recomputed
coverage added points at 6.10 and 8.35. Pooling the 1.5B/ce arms of both gives
accuracy flat to within the suite MDE for every C2 <= 8.35 and then 43.87 at
14.47 and 8.19 at 39.15. Nothing is measured between 8.35 and 14.47, which is
exactly where the shape of the relationship is decided.
Design. One student (Qwen2.5-1.5B), one objective (ce, where G3 found the effect
largest), one teacher (7B-Instruct), seven coverage levels, three seeds each.
The levels come from a (fraction x drop-seed) grid over corpus.mask_fraction's
cell_drop mode, whose C2 was MEASURED BEFORE ANY TRAINING and which is not
monotone in the fraction, because dropping a heavy cell and dropping a light one
move C2 very differently. Selecting levels on that pre-measured C2 is selection
on a property of the design, not on the outcome -- the same logic as G3's
capacity probe.
The confound that has to be removed. Across the grid, C2 and the number of
supervised positions are strongly anti-correlated: 163438 positions at C2=7.8
against 117354 at C2=19.4. Left alone, the sweep would vary coverage and
supervision quantity together. All arms are therefore matched down to the common
floor of the selected set, and C2 is re-measured AFTER matching, since matching
removes positions and can move the coefficient.
What the stage cannot do. Seven levels and three seeds locate a changepoint to
within one step of the ladder at best. A reported threshold is 'between these
two measured levels', never a point estimate.
REVISION 11 (recorded, not hidden): a new stage G10 is registered, with the
thresholds in the g10 block above written BEFORE any arm ran.
What it tests, and why it is needed. Twenty-one supervision measures have now been
trained on the same student with the same objective. Nineteen land at 64.6-67.6%
accuracy while C2 over the full 1296-state abstraction varies by a factor of
nineteen (1.01 to 19.45); two collapse, to 43.87% and 8.19%. So C2 AS THIS WORK
DEFINES IT DOES NOT SEPARATE THEM, and the earlier reading of a threshold in C2
is withdrawn. Four positional statistics do separate all twenty-one perfectly, the
cleanest being the coverage of the worst-covered step-position bucket: at most
0.0003 for the two that collapse against at least 0.1824 for the nineteen that do
not. Notably the separating statistic includes C2 itself computed on the 6-state
step-position marginal rather than on all 1296 states, which by the data
processing inequality is a LOWER bound on the full coefficient -- coarsening helps,
because variation across magnitude and operation cells swamps the positional
signal.
That separation was found after seeing which configurations collapsed, and rests
on two collapsing cases, so it is exploratory. G10 tests it forward with a dial
that targets the statistic directly, and with a second factor that discriminates
between two accounts: the hole is placed in an EARLY step bucket or a LATE one at
the same measured coverage. A magnitude account predicts no difference. A
positional account predicts that starving early positions is far worse, which is
what the existing masks hint at -- supervising only the last quarter of each trace
costs 22 points while supervising only the first quarter costs 0.4.
Supervised steps are matched to a common floor across all eight cells, and the
achieved coverage is measured after matching rather than assumed from the rate.
REVISION 12 (recorded, not hidden): stage G11, thresholds above written
BEFORE any arm ran. It exists because the statistic G10 was built to test turned
out to be the wrong one, and the file records that.
What went wrong. The post-hoc separation of the twenty-one trained configurations
used min_cov_step: the coverage of the WORST step bucket. A minimum is blind to
how many buckets are starved, and the two datasets differ on exactly that. G3's
`late` mask leaves bucket 1 at 0.000 AND bucket 2 at 0.035 -- two early buckets --
while G10's early arm throttles bucket 1 alone, because step_bucket(t)=min(t+1,5)
makes bucket 1 the first step only. G10's arms are flat from min_cov 0.019 to
0.154, so the statistic does not carry the effect at the depths tested.
What the per-bucket vectors show instead. The `early` mask leaves bucket 5 at
0.182 -- 65% of the teacher's occupancy mass covered at 18% -- and loses nothing
(65.43%). So starved MASS is not the driver either: a thin LATE region is
harmless while a thin EARLY region is not. Any statistic that is symmetric across
step position, min or sum alike, cannot express this.
What G11 tests. Two readings survive and they are distinguishable. DEPTH: an early
bucket needs some nonzero supervision, and 1.9% suffices while 0% does not.
BREADTH: one starved early bucket is survivable, two or more is not. Three cells
separate them, and all four outcomes -- depth, breadth, both required, neither --
are reportable.

_note_rank_split: Estimator A coarsens 64 states into 16 cells, so it is held to a lower rank
bar than B and C, which see state identity. Holding a coarse estimator to a
fine estimator's bar blames it for a property of its feature map.

superseded_thresholds.note: was a gate; now reported as gain_min_points_diagnostic

g3.interaction_capacity_sign: coverage effect larger for the larger student

g9._what: Does the coverage effect have a THRESHOLD or is it GRADUAL? Pre-registered before any arm ran; both outcomes are reportable.
g9._cliff_ratio: largest drop between adjacent C2 levels, divided by the mean of the remaining adjacent drops.  >= 3.0 is read as a threshold; < 3.0 is read as a gradual decline.  Neither is a failure of the stage -- the stage exists to tell the two apart.

g10._what: Is it the MAGNITUDE of the coverage hole, or WHERE the hole is? Registered before any arm ran; both outcomes are reportable.
g10._g10_1: At the tightest coverage target, accuracy with a LATE step bucket starved minus accuracy with an EARLY one starved, in points. The magnitude account predicts about zero: both have the same coverage. The positional account predicts a large positive number.
g10._g10_2: Within the early-starved series, Spearman of measured coverage against accuracy over four levels.

g11._what: Does the collapse need a DEEP hole in one early step bucket, or a BROAD hole across several? Registered before any arm ran; all outcomes report.
g11._cells: b1@0.001 (depth), b1b2@0.02 (breadth), b1b2b3b4@0.02 (breadth, wider). Matched to the same 67637-step floor as G10 so the numbers compare.
g11._read: A cell counts as collapsed if it loses at least 10 points against the G10 early/0.02 reference of 66.60%. Depth wins if only cell 1 collapses; breadth wins if cell 2 or 3 collapses while cell 1 does not; if none collapses, the collapse needs both and the hypothesis is narrower still.

g12._what: The early-vs-late gap is the only clean contrast in G3 (identical row sets, 37509 supervised steps, 2.37 steps/row, 11.67 trace length, 0.216 ratio, +0.893 corr, 99.9% teacher-cache). It is worth 21.6 points at 1.5B/ce. This stage asks WHY, by moving a fraction f of each trace's own supervision budget from the back of the trace to the front. Registered before any arm ran; every outcome reports.
g12._design: Per trace of m steps the budget is k=max(1,round(0.25*m)) -- exactly the k that G3's early and late masks use -- of which round(f*k) steps are taken from the front and the remainder from the back. So f=0 reproduces late and f=1 reproduces early, and every arm is matched on row set, supervised step count, steps per row, trace length and supervision-to-length ratio by construction. The only variable is WHERE inside each trace the budget sits.
g12._replication: f=0 must land within 3.0 points of G3's late (43.87%) and f=1 within 3.0 points of G3's early (65.43%), both at 1.5B/ce. If either fails, the stage is void and reports as a failed replication, not as evidence about mechanism.
g12._read: Let d_first = acc(f=1/3) - acc(f=0) and d_last = acc(f=1) - acc(f=2/3). PREFIX REPAIR if d_first >= 2.0*d_last: the first slice of early supervision buys disproportionately, which is what a compounding-error account predicts, because the student cannot use a late-step skill it never reaches. PROPORTIONAL if |d_first - d_last| <= MDE (2.13 points): the effect scales with how much of the budget sits early, i.e. early steps simply carry more learnable signal and there is no special prefix role. LATE SATURATION if d_last >= 2.0*d_first, the opposite shape. Anything else reports as MIXED.
g12._REPLICATION_CRITERION_WAS_UNSATISFIABLE: Recorded 2026-11-02, after the sweep ran. The criterion above -- f=0 within 3.0 points of G3's late (43.87) -- FAILED: f=0 came out at 30.03. We report that failure as registered and do not read the shape result as confirmatory. But the criterion could never have been met. G3's late arm has a seed standard deviation of 11.94 (per-seed 61.80, 43.04, 28.38, 41.20, 44.92), so a +-3.0 point 95% interval needs about 122 seeds; with three seeds the half-width is 19.17 points. A Welch test of the two means gives t = 2.01, df = 5.9, p = 0.091: the two are not distinguishable. Setting a 3-point tolerance on the noisiest arm in the study was an error in this file, not a result. The arm's instability was already documented in the conference paper before this threshold was written.
g12._what_would_settle_it: Two things, both of which must be declared as a revision rather than applied retroactively. (a) More seeds on f000 only, which is the only unstable arm: the others have standard deviations of 0.76, 0.38 and 0.07. (b) A replication criterion stated as a statistical test -- f=0 not distinguishable from G3's late at p < 0.05 -- instead of a fixed tolerance. Under (b) the present data already passes, which is exactly why it must not be adopted after seeing them.

_observed_2026_11_02.registered_reading: PREFIX REPAIR (d_first >= 2 * d_last, and above MDE)
_observed_2026_11_02.status: EXPLORATORY: the replication gate failed as registered

_REVISION_13: Added g12: the reallocation sweep that tests the mechanism behind the clean early-vs-late gap. Registered 2026-10-26, before any g12 arm ran.
_REVISION_14: g12 ran. The registered replication gate failed and the stage is reported as exploratory. Recorded that the gate was unsatisfiable by construction, with the power calculation, rather than quietly relaxing it. 2026-11-02.
